linear.dependency_representation: Prerequisites are recorded in descriptions. F14 additionally has native blocker F22 (ASC-43); F22 has native blocker F05 (ASC-9). Other native blocker relationships have not been configured.

milestones.name: 01 Integration setup — Month 1
milestones.description: Prepare development inputs, exercise compiler continuation, configure one supported comparison route and verify the selected agent harness.

milestones.name: 02 Baseline implementation — Months 2–3
milestones.description: Implement the narrow end-to-end baseline in Python 3.15+, including durable state, runner contracts, agent file editing, configured comparison and feedback.

milestones.name: 03 MVP — Month 4
milestones.description: Complete runnable finding bundles, replay, recovery and end-to-end MVP acceptance.

tasks.title: Prepare AscendNPU-IR development fixtures and execution assets
tasks.scope: Package existing engineer-supplied kernels or IR fragments for integration development and smoke tests.
acceptance: Record original code, enclosing context, inputs, reference results and harness commands.
Record compiler/target versions, required access and missing execution assets.
Provide one documented fixture layout with reproducible setup instructions.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.1–2.2

tasks.title: Verify AscendNPU-IR compilation entry and stopping points
tasks.scope: Exercise the intended saved-IR input and continuation commands on a development fixture; document the integration contract.
acceptance: Demonstrate the intended compiler entry point and required input state.
Record output checkpoints and hard stop boundaries with commands and diagnostics.
Record required metadata, compiler version, target and execution resources; report unsupported configurations.
sources: questions/Q08 - Compilation continuation and validation routes.md

tasks.title: Configure the MVP compilation, validation and metric route
tasks.scope: Encode the selected MVP compiler, checking process and metric as an executable configuration. Tool and metric selection remain external prerequisites until resolved; this task does not perform a comparative research study.
acceptance: Record the selected start/output checkpoints, checks, evaluator and their versions.
Provide commands, required inputs, environment bindings and hardware requirements for the route.
Verify joint compatibility and preserve separate correctness and improvement results; report unresolved selections as blockers.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4
questions/Q06 - Metrics for assessing LLVM IR and MLIR improvements.md
questions/Q08 - Compilation continuation and validation routes.md

tasks.title: Demonstrate a reproducible original/candidate comparison
tasks.scope: Exercise the selected compiler, checking policy and metric on a supplied original and alternative before building full orchestration. Preserve commands and artifacts for the later shared execution recipe.
acceptance: Compile both versions under the same resolved settings.
Record independent check outcomes, metric values and applicability limits.
Retain a reproducible comparison and diagnose failures explicitly.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4

tasks.title: Verify the agent harness can read and edit an AscendNPU-IR working copy
tasks.scope: Exercise the selected agent backend with ordinary file reading/editing against one development fixture before implementing durable orchestration.
acceptance: Document backend setup and record prompt/profile and model configuration.
Capture the edited file, framework-visible messages and tool results through the harness.
Submit the captured version to the F04 comparison route and document interface errors or unsupported capabilities.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.2–2.3

tasks.title: Configure Python 3.15 development tooling and package setup
tasks.scope: Complete the development environment inside framework/ using the current Python 3.15 series. The initial directory and metadata are only scaffolding.
acceptance: Provide reproducible environment/package setup using the pinned interpreter.
Choose and document dependency management, formatting, type checks and meaningful test commands.
Keep virtual environments, caches, secrets and generated run artifacts out of Git.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2

tasks.title: Implement request, profile and outcome data contracts
tasks.scope: Translate the agreed H03 contracts into versioned Python data models and serialization. Implement the selected MVP subset explicitly.
acceptance: Resolve defaults → request → per-input settings while preserving shared limits.
Represent compilation, checking, metric, target, agent and budget configuration.
Reject missing/unsupported configurations and preserve independent outcome/coverage records.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.1, §2.4

tasks.title: Implement immutable input snapshots and editing-scope enforcement
tasks.scope: Prepare an investigation case and an agent working copy tied to immutable original artifacts. Supporting context remains distinct from editable code.
acceptance: Persist original artifacts, supplied context and selection provenance.
Support the selected whole-input or specified-range MVP mode with explicit boundaries.
Detect edits outside the allowed scope and produce candidate snapshots plus framework-generated diffs.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.1–2.3

tasks.title: Implement durable investigation, artifact and operation storage
tasks.scope: Persist the complete investigation chain rather than relying on temporary directories or a live agent session. Choose concrete storage during implementation.
acceptance: Assign stable investigation/case/candidate/operation identifiers and retain artifact references.
Record operation intent, state, effective configuration, evidence and budget consumption/reservations.
Publish artifacts durably before completion checkpoints; retain transcripts and visible tool records.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.5

tasks.title: Implement the selected compilation runner
tasks.scope: Compile one original or candidate version per invocation using the route established during feasibility.
acceptance: Accept snapshot, enclosing context, checkpoint, pipeline, target and limits.
Return artifact manifests, actual invocation, diagnostics and available resource use.
Distinguish baseline failure, candidate compiler rejection, timeout, unsupported request and infrastructure failure.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4

tasks.title: Implement the selected validation adapter
tasks.scope: Execute the selected MVP checking policy and record the behavior or invariants covered.
acceptance: Handle references, test material, tolerances, assumptions and environment requirements.
Represent passed/failed/inconclusive/unsupported/error/not-performed outcomes independently.
Preserve observed differences, coverage and diagnostics; compilation-only evidence receives its own label.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4
questions/Q08 - Compilation continuation and validation routes.md

tasks.title: Implement the selected metric evaluator and comparison criterion
tasks.scope: Assess corresponding original/candidate artifacts through the metric configured in F03. Preserve its stage, coverage and interpretation.
acceptance: Record evaluator version, units, raw values, conditions and any measurement protocol.
Apply configured improvement direction and threshold.
Report unsupported coverage or inconclusive assessment explicitly; static scores retain their limited interpretation.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4
questions/Q06 - Metrics for assessing LLVM IR and MLIR improvements.md

tasks.title: Implement the shared comparison recipe for evaluation and replay
tasks.scope: Coordinate the compiler, validator and evaluator through one versioned execution recipe used both initially and when replaying a finding.
acceptance: Check route compatibility and enforce observation/stopping settings without silent substitutions.
Retain independent validation and metric outcomes with the selected finding-eligibility rules.
Reuse applicable original results under explicit compatibility rules and checkpoint each completed operation.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4, §2.6

tasks.title: Implement the agent session and working-copy adapter
tasks.scope: Integrate the backend exercised in F05. Provide prepared code/context and ordinary file editing through the selected harness. Integrate the versioned dialect reference pack and knowledge-delivery path from F22; record supplied/retrieved semantics and context limitations.
acceptance: Version prompts and record effective model/backend settings.
Persist framework-visible conversation, tool results, candidate versions and optional agent notes.
Enforce edit scope, preserve complete artifacts for checking and report context limitations.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.2–2.3

tasks.title: Implement feedback, budget enforcement and default stopping
tasks.scope: Connect agent proposals to comparison evidence and continue the same conversation for repairs or new attempts within the configured budget.
acceptance: Return structured feedback distinguishing code problems, coverage limits and infrastructure failures.
Compare each candidate to the unchanged original; stop at the first qualifying finding, exhausted limits or inability to proceed.
Preserve each attempt, best eligible result and used/reserved budget; do not reset limits on restart.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.5

tasks.title: Expose the baseline investigation through a CLI
tasks.scope: Provide the selected engineer-supplied-input workflow from framework/. Concrete command syntax can be finalized during implementation.
acceptance: Accept request/profile paths and explicit supporting material.
Report missing requirements, progress, result locations and operation failures.
Document an executable example using the chosen route and configuration.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.1–2.5

tasks.title: Export runnable finding bundles and a replay command
tasks.scope: Package successful comparisons as independent runnable experiments using the shared recipe rather than requiring agent rediscovery.
acceptance: Export original/candidate code, diff, recipe, checks, metric evidence, environment bindings and a concise report.
Use bundle-local references and publish complete exports with stable finding IDs.
Replay through the same execution path and store fresh results without overwriting original evidence.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.6

tasks.title: Implement investigation resume and interrupted-operation reconciliation
tasks.scope: Recover durable progress, working copies and agent context after internal failures. Handle uncertain external work explicitly.
acceptance: Reuse completed applicable operations and reconcile recorded job IDs or artifacts.
Restore a session where supported or reconstruct context from persisted records.
Preserve findings and budgets; distinguish candidate repair from infrastructure retry and account for uncertain work.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.5

tasks.title: Verify finding replay after relocation
tasks.scope: Exercise exported findings independently of the generating worker, temporary directory and live agent session.
acceptance: Replay from a relocated bundle using declared external bindings.
Report missing dependencies/hardware and retain divergent or failed replay outcomes.
Verify interrupted export recovery and fresh requested validation/metric results.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.6
questions/H08 - How will we check success.md

tasks.title: Verify end-to-end failure handling, recovery and evidence boundaries
tasks.scope: Add integration checks for the meaningful failure cases in the selected route and orchestration, using recorded or deterministic fixtures where appropriate.
acceptance: Cover baseline/candidate compilation failure, unsupported/inconclusive checks, mismatches and non-improvement.
Interrupt at durable boundaries and verify reuse, restored context and preserved budget.
Verify out-of-scope edits and incompatible routes cannot become ready findings.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.4–2.6

tasks.title: Verify the complete MVP workflow on an AscendNPU-IR case
tasks.scope: Run the supported engineer-supplied-input workflow using real development material and verify its technical acceptance requirements.
acceptance: Run input preparation, agent editing, compilation, checks, metric comparison and feedback under configured limits.
Export and replay an eligible comparison; use a known qualifying fixture if the search produces none, clearly recording its provenance.
Interrupt and resume an investigation, then document executable setup/run/replay/resume instructions and remaining integration limitations.
Exercise F22 (ASC-43): record the versioned dialect knowledge supplied or retrieved by the agent, supported operation coverage and unresolved semantic assumptions.
sources: questions/H07 - How long will it take.md
questions/H08 - How will we check success.md

tasks.title: Deliver AscendNPU-IR dialect knowledge to the agent for the MVP
tasks.scope: Make the selected AscendNPU-IR representation usable by the agent through versioned, source-grounded instructions, reference material and file access. Dialect coverage and a working knowledge-delivery path are MVP requirements; comparative prompt/retrieval optimization remains separate research.
acceptance: Define the supported checkpoint/dialect/operation subset and curate a versioned reference pack from authoritative specifications, compiler definitions and engineer-reviewed examples. Include types, attributes, operation semantics/effects, target constraints and known unsupported or undocumented behavior.

Implement one knowledge-delivery path: concise entry instructions plus relevant reference material in context or readable files through the selected harness. Record what was supplied or retrieved, source versions and context limitations; expose unresolved semantics rather than inventing facts.

Exercise the full path on representative AscendNPU-IR fixtures: capture the model-visible material and rewritten MLIR, run available verification/compilation and selected checks, and have an engineer review semantic assumptions. Make the supported scope and remaining gaps explicit in MVP acceptance.
sources: questions/H03 - What is new in our approach.md §2.2–2.3
questions/Q09 - Agent prompt construction and information delivery.md

scope: Technical setup, implementation and engineering verification only. Research studies and pitch work are outside this backlog.
